restrictions: Messages are exactly 64 bytes: eight 32-bit point lanes followed by eight 32-bit salt lanes, little-endian.
Single salted van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point rho walk of exactly k=2^128+2^40 compressions; no restart.
Relocation from x_0 with known lag: at most k' applications to form b=f^lambda(x_0) and at most k' lockstep iterations; fail if lambda>k'.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256; 2 prefix rounds; one 64-byte root block with flags 11, length 64, counter 0.
Classical 256-bit word RAM; distinguished when point lane 0 is zero (theta=2^-32); D_max=2^110 records of 64 bytes each.
Success probability 0.39 depends on score-critical heuristic H1-salted-random-mapping; time and memory caps are worst-case and heuristic-free.
Analytical generic construction near the birthday bound; no full-scale execution or precomputed collision is claimed.
Revision of refuted 1e53125f: charges birthday-scale relocation, corrects cycle-length analysis, and prices records at 64 bytes.
The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over 128; the claimed scalar 130.18 is a charged-overhead bound above the birthday exponent.

heuristics.statement: For a uniformly random salt and an independent uniform start point, the failure probability of the distinguished-point rho events A,B,D,E,F,G on the real salted 2-round BLAKE3 walk map f_s is at most the corresponding probability for a uniform random function on 2^256 points, up to a negligible additive gap covered by the 0.0034 allowance between the random-function bound (>0.3934) and the claimed success probability 0.39.
heuristics.scope: Applies only to the success-probability claim for this salted single-trail DP-rho algorithm with the stated parameters (k'=2^128, theta=2^-32, g=2^40, D_max=2^110, relocation caps lambda<=k' and lockstep<=k'). It does not assert anything about unsalted fixed maps, parallel multi-trail statistics beyond the charged single walk, differential cryptanalysis, or sub-birthday structure.
heuristics.extrapolation: The organizer-scaled experiment uses a 16-bit truncation of the same 2-round root compression with proportional DP parameters and the same relocation caps (lambda<=k', lockstep<=k'). Agreeing rho statistics there, together with the standard generic-hash modeling premise for salted walks, are extrapolated across about 240 bits of digest to the full 256-bit map. No proof rules out a global permutation-like structure that would suppress collisions. Relative slack g/k' is larger at the 16-bit scale than at full scale; that mismatch is disclosed and is why the scaled frequency is only supporting evidence.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is not proved. Truncated experiments cannot detect global injectivity or other large-structure deviations of the full map. The 0.0034 allowance above 0.39 is not statistically certified at full scale. Only the scaled experiment is organizer-executed; no full-scale collision is known. A map closer to a permutation would lower success probability below the claim. The scaled g/k' ratio exceeds the full-scale ratio.
